messages.subject: Re: struggle with [, , drop=FALSE] for matrix with one colun
parts:
Hi Ryan,
From the code you give in the question, I do not see why you have to use a one-column matrix for ug instead of simply a vector, if n.utraits = 1. I am not sure about the other part of the model, so, it would be useful if you give a more complete example, or you can try to use a vector instead of matrix in your code. It might also help if you add one more column of 0's to both ug and utraits and let n.utraits = 2 - this does not affect the result of mu.u.b

Best wishes,
Wei

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: struggle with [, , drop=FALSE] for matrix with one colun
parts:
A note that if you use `drop=FALSE` then you are passing matrices (since it won't drop either dimension) as the arguments to `inprod`, which is not allowed.

As far as your original attempt, it looks like we don't support having 1-element vectors (e.g., `x[1:1]`) as arguments to `inprod`. I would think we'd want that to work for the generalizability reason that you mention, so I'll file an issue for us to look into that.

-chris
